replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I love math because it’s logical and creative, like solving puzzles. As a student in Milan, I find it practical for everyday problems and connects to art through patterns. My parents’ different educational backgrounds made me appreciate math’s accessibility.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I rarely get anxious about math, but sometimes when problems feel too complex or time-sensitive. My neuroticism score is high, so I try to break tasks into small steps. I use gardening to relax and refocus when stressed.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used AI tools like ChatGPT to check my solutions and understand concepts. It helped clarify tricky topics but sometimes gave confusing answers. I learned to verify results with textbooks and my teacher.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant b² - 4ac. If it’s positive, you get two real solutions; zero gives one solution; negative gives complex ones. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the derivative f’(x). Set it equal to zero and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points could be maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
